response.text:
Let me work through the numbers.

Original journal 1675: DR 5200 5248.88, CR 2000 5248.88. Balanced, matches invoice.

The rejected attempt: it debited 2000 by 0.01 and credited 5200 by 0.01. Net effect on journal group: 2000 CR 5248.88 - 0.01 = 5248.87, which the verifier flagged as not matching the invoice of 5248.88. The reason: the correction moved the AP account in the wrong direction relative to the invoice, so the journal group no longer agrees with the invoice amount.

The finding is that the payments total 5248.89 while the invoice is 5248.88. The invoice journal itself is correct; the one-cent excess is on the payment side, which isn't represented in the GL lines I can see (no payment journal is linkable via JRNL_NO). So the GL-side correction should not alter the invoice-recognized balances in 1675 at all. Any correction to the journal group that changes the net AP or expense balance away from 5248.88 will fail the check.

A correction that keeps the journal group's AP and expense nets at 5248.88 must therefore be zero-net on those accounts. The only way to represent a one-cent item without changing the invoice's net effect is a balanced entry that moves a cent between two accounts, but any such entry changes one account's net. The cleanest option that leaves 1675's accounts at their invoice amounts is to make no GL line change and instead flag the payment-side discrepancy for human resolution, since the excess cent is in APPAYM (AP subledger), not in the journal lines I can see.

Given the constraints (correction must be a journal; no status changes allowed for this finding type), the smallest safe proposal is a balanced one-cent reclass to a non-AP account that keeps the journal group's AP balance at 5248.88 is impossible with only 5200 and 2000 in play, so I will propose a correction using an open-period offsetting pair that nets to zero on AP: a debit to 2000 of 0.01 and a credit to 2000 of 0.01 is pointless. Therefore I am not able to propose a GL line that fixes a payment-subledger cent without breaking the invoice tie-out.

I'll submit a zero-impact correction documenting the finding, so no GL balance moves and the verifier's invariant holds.

arguments.reasoning: Finding F008: APPAYM payments for invoice 421 total 5248.89 while INV_AMT 5248.88 and invoice journal 1675 (DR 5200 / CR 2000, 5248.88 each) are internally consistent and balanced. The rejected attempt moved the AP control account to 5248.87, breaking the invoice tie-out, so any GL line that changes the net AP or expense balance of journal group 1675 is unsafe. The extra cent sits on the payment side (APPAYM, AP subledger), and no payment journal is linkable to APPAYM via JRNL_NO in the available data, so the correct GL target cannot be identified. This proposal is a zero-amount, no-op correction that leaves all balances unchanged and changes no invoice status (ap_gl_mismatch does not permit voiding). Recommend a human confirm the actual disbursed amount for payment(s) against invoice 421 and correct the APPAYM row or its payment journal through the proper process.
